reason: Per-agent caps, a human-review queue and a kill switch in front of our own MCP server are something my team can build inside a quarter, so by default we build it. Even in shadow mode this is an unaudited startup's proxy sitting inline on our order path, and that's not where I take a chance, competitor announcement or not.
objection: It's another hop in the order path: added latency and a new single point of failure from a vendor with no customers and no SOC 2. If it hiccups, my matching flow hiccups. Also, a FINRA and MAS SAFR mapping doesn't speak to how a US crypto venue actually gets examined.
would_change_my_mind: A true out-of-path shadow mode that reads a mirrored copy of our MCP traffic asynchronously, plus published p99 latency and fail-open/fail-closed behavior for when we switch on enforcement.
